criteria.evidence: attention-rows.ts words run-stalled, run-looping and run-overspending (one row each, id includes the kind, action 'View run' to /runs/<id>); bureau-attention.ts keeps the three kinds (KNOWN_ATTENTION_KINDS). Tests: attention-rows.test.ts (4 new), bureau-attention.test.ts (kinds kept). Home's own Needs attention card is untouched (its KIND_ORDER leaves them out, as worker-disconnected); Health's list is the one worded.

RunRow.attention (taskRow, instance rows carry the union of their steps' states); run-list-row.svelte draws one Badge per state through StackedListItem's badge slot (warning for stalled and looping, danger for overspending); the slot's gap is Cinder's (stacked-list-item.css, asserted in stacked-list-item-badge.test.ts). Tests: run-rows-attention.test.ts, run-list-attention.test.ts.

Cinder's ToggleFacet 'Needs attention' chip; the address holds attention=1 (parseRunFilter/serializeRunFilter, kept when another filter changes); with it on the page reads listAllTasksNeedingAttention, one bureau.tasks.list per kind (stalled, looping, overspending) merged by task, and no unfiltered page-of-100 listing. A settled run that overspent is listed. Steps are listed as themselves under the filter so an instance is never built from some of its steps. Tests: run-list-attention.test.ts (asserts the three attention requests and the settled run), run-rows-attention.test.ts.

run-attention-note.svelte (Callout, warning, one per state) under the Run page header: states the condition for stalled, looping and overspending; a stalled run says when the Bureau saw it stall and that it last made progress before then. The wire carries only the instant the stall was seen (run-bookkeeping.ts records that instant, never the last pulse), so the copy states it as a bound, not as the last-progress time. Tests: run-attention-note.test.ts.

The field shipped with COR-2527 (settings-controls.ts, runs.spendThresholdUsd in General).
